nodes.label: Evidence-Ranked Diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Product edits wait until evidence supports one credible causal mechanism.

nodes.label: Narrow Observable Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Feature work stops at a coherent end-to-end outcome and omits speculative modes, services, configuration, and polish.

nodes.label: Reuse Fitting Seam
nodes.rationale: Existing ownership seams are preferred unless patching them would duplicate behavior or hide the root cause.

nodes.label: Narrowest Responsible Layer
nodes.rationale: The smallest correct fix changes the layer that owns the faulty mechanism and avoids unrelated cleanup.

nodes.label: Smallest Sufficient Proof Set
nodes.rationale: Validation stops immediately after acceptance is proven and does not expand into cleanup or unrelated testing.

nodes.label: Caveman Auto-Clarity
nodes.rationale: Temporarily restores normal prose where compression could make safety or ordering ambiguous.

nodes.label: User Language Preservation
nodes.rationale: Compression changes style but must not switch the user's language or remove grammatical markers needed for meaning.

nodes.label: Technical Integrity Under Compression
nodes.rationale: Compression removes filler while retaining negation, exact technical terms, numbers, code, and error strings.

nodes.label: Reversible Compatibility-Safe Transition
nodes.rationale: Migration design preserves data, supports mixed versions, makes retries safe, and keeps rollback available.

nodes.label: Behavior Preservation Boundary
nodes.rationale: Verification brackets structural edits so interfaces, ordering, failures, and compatibility remain unchanged.

nodes.label: Rule Overhead and Net Savings
nodes.rationale: Reports rule input overhead and net savings to expose workloads where terse output costs more overall.

nodes.label: Session Log Token Measurement
nodes.rationale: Reads JSONL session logs so usage figures come from recorded data rather than model estimation.

nodes.label: Deterministic Node IDs
nodes.rationale: Full repository-relative paths and normalized entity names keep semantic output aligned with AST extraction and incremental replacement.

nodes.label: Existing Graph Fast Path
nodes.rationale: Natural-language codebase questions use an existing graph immediately to avoid unnecessary extraction and clustering.

nodes.label: Graph Health Check
nodes.rationale: A read-only integrity gate exposes dangling, missing, self-loop, and collapsed edges without making a usable graph unavailable.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: Queries are expanded only with vocabulary present in graph node labels because the CLI has no stemming, synonym, or cross-language matching and literal wording mismatches otherwise yield irrelevant or empty results.

nodes.label: Dirty Graph Output Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Hook and incremental-update changes in graphify-out are expected and should not prevent graph use unless the task concerns stale output or the user opts out.

nodes.label: Graph-First Codebase Workflow
nodes.rationale: Scoped graph query, path, and explain commands should be used before broad reports or raw source searches because they return smaller, more relevant subgraphs.

nodes.label: Code-Only Update Fast Path
nodes.rationale: When all changed files are code, deterministic AST extraction is sufficient and semantic extraction can be skipped without API or LLM cost.

nodes.label: Semantic Manifest Stamping
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped so failed chunks are re-queued on the next update instead of being silently treated as complete.

nodes.label: Whisper Domain Hint
nodes.rationale: A short hint derived from graph concepts improves transcription vocabulary and punctuation without requiring a separate API call.

nodes.label: Monorepo Subgraph Extraction
nodes.rationale: Each local subfolder must write its own graphify-out directory because running the skill repeatedly from the project root would clobber the shared output directory.

nodes.label: Authenticated Service Exploration
nodes.rationale: Store and menu discovery is restricted to logged-in users, while logged-out users can access only login and signup screens.

nodes.label: Checkout Without PG Payment
nodes.rationale: The current version displays checkout and payment confirmation UI but excludes actual payment-gateway integration.

nodes.label: Location Fallback Search
nodes.rationale: Users must still be able to discover stores through search when current-location information is unavailable.

nodes.label: Single-Store Cart
nodes.rationale: A cart may contain products from only one store; adding a product from another store requires confirmation that the existing cart will be cleared.
